explain.say: Toner is a fine plastic powder that is also charged. It sticks only to the parts the laser touched, and then the paper, given a stronger opposite charge, pulls the powder off the drum.

faq.q: Why does a laser printer use static electricity?
faq.a: Static charge can hold powder in place without touching it. The drum is coated in a material that holds charge in the dark but lets it drain away where light hits, so light can draw a charge pattern.
asks: How does static make a printed page?

faq.q: What does the laser do in a laser printer?
faq.a: The laser switches on and off millions of times a second as a spinning mirror sweeps it across the drum. Wherever it shines, the charge drains away, drawing the text and pictures as an invisible charge pattern.
asks: Why is it called a laser printer?

faq.a: Toner is an extremely fine powder made mostly of plastic with colour pigment. It is not ink: it is held in place by static and then melted onto the paper.
asks: Is toner the same as ink?

faq.q: Why is paper warm from a laser printer?
faq.a: The fuser's hot rollers, at roughly 200 degrees Celsius, melt the plastic toner and press it into the paper fibres so it cannot rub off. The paper is still warm when it comes out.

faq.q: Why is a laser printer faster than an inkjet?
faq.a: A laser printer draws a whole page in one smooth pass of the drum instead of moving a print head back and forth line by line, so it can print dozens of pages a minute.
asks: Laser or inkjet, which is better?

facts: Gary Starkweather developed the laser printer at Xerox in 1969 to 1971.
Laser printing is based on xerography, invented by Chester Carlson in 1938.
